\# Reflection

This Human Subjects Research training through CITI helped me better understand the responsibilities a researcher has towards his/her subjects in human subjects research. Before starting the modules I had thought of research as fair and as responsible but after starting the modules I realized that there are many more principles and rules to follow in order to conduct research in an ethical manner.

The topic of informed consent was well described in the modules, and this was one of the most important concepts for me to understand. I now have a clear understanding of the information that must be given to potential participants in order for them to make an informed decision regarding participation in a research study. This includes a clear description of the study for which they are considering participation, the potential risks and benefits to them, how information will be kept confidential, and their rights as participants including their right to withdraw from the study at any time without any penalty.

Protecting Privacy and Maintaining Confidentiality – The researcher has a responsibility to protect the privacy of participants and maintain confidentiality of information collected during research. Researchers must take steps to ensure data are stored in a secure manner and only granted access to by individuals who require such to complete aspects of the research. Where possible, steps must also be taken to protect the identity of the participant(s) in any analysis conducted as part of the research.

This module also helped me to better understand the researcher’s responsibility to identify and minimize risks to participants in a research study. Even seemingly innocuous research can potentially cause discomfort or even harm to a participant(s) in some way. Thus, researchers must carefully weigh potential risks to participants against the potential benefits of their research.

The CITI program also explained the role of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) for protecting human subjects involved in research studies. IRBs ensure that proposed and ongoing research utilizing human subjects comply with generally accepted principles for the protection of human research participants, and approve research prior to the start of data collection.

As a graduate student, completing this training will help me be an even better student and enhance my ability to do good research and complete school projects of all kinds. This will aid me in remaining responsible and completing quality school work in all of my future academic endeavors.

The entire CITI course was useful in strengthening my knowledge on the concepts and responsibilities that come with gathering information and making decisions about individuals and organizations involved in research. These will be applicable not only in academics but also in professional settings where data is collected for research purposes.
